## The question this category answers

> How do you issue a unit that holds a peg when its backing is volatile, held by someone else, and can become worth less than the unit?

## The category residue the original lane recorded

Two structural failures. (1) Monetary policy. Every protocol here sets a rate to defend a peg — Sky's Stability Fee and SSR, USDD's Stability Fees, Lista's, crvUSD's automatic controller, Liquity V2's borrower-chosen rates. The vocabulary's Stability register contains Rd, Ps and As: a redemption right, a 1:1 swap, and quantity adjustment. There is no price-of-credit instrument in it at all, and that is the instrument all five actually use. (2) The synthetic-dollar family is outside the register entirely. Ethena ($3,873M) + Falcon Finance ($1,253M) + Solstice ($507M) = $5,633M, which is larger than Sky, and none of them are CDPs: the backing is a hedged position on venues the protocol does not control. Expressing that family needs at minimum three new elements — off-exchange custody/mirroring, off-protocol revenue capture, and a maintained-neutrality invariant — none of which exist even as candidates. Separately: Sky, USDD and Lista CDP form a strict nesting (Lista subset-of USDD subset-of Sky, differing only by At, Xf and Fd), so three protocols and $7.3B collapse into one Maker skeleton the vocabulary cannot tell apart. The Dutch auction used by all three is reachable only through contested Da, which given 3-of-5 usage is the strongest promotion candidate in the contested register. And Frax, named in the brief as an exemplar, is now $42.6M and filed by DefiLlama under 'Algo-Stables' — the algorithmic design As was presumably written for has left the top of the market entirely.

### Residue, verbatim

**Ethena (USDe / sUSDe)** (9):

- the right to create or destroy the unit is suspended automatically whenever the unit's price diverges unfavourably from its stablecoin reference beyond a configured threshold
- creation and destruction are capped per block, separately for stablecoin and non-stablecoin assets, under a global cap adjustable by a development multisig
- the backing is a book of six strategy families — crypto basis, non-crypto basis, DeFi lending, institutional lending, tokenised real-world assets and liquid stablecoins — whose allocation across categories is changed continuously at the operator's discretion
- the protocol's revenue is the funding payment of perpetual markets it does not operate and does not govern, received as an ordinary external participant
- the backing never sits on the venue that holds the hedge: it is held by named third-party settlement providers in bankruptcy-remote structures and only delegated to derivatives venues as margin on a rolling four-hour cycle, so that on a venue's failure positions are treated as closed and exposure is limited to unsettled profit and loss between cycles
- the prices used to quote creation and redemption are computed by an off-chain service that ingests six centralised venues plus two oracle networks, normalises and validates them, and publishes the result; no contract reads a price feed to test solvency
- the level of the payout is decided off-chain: a foundation subsidiary calculates an annual percentage yield weekly as part of internal accounting and executes it as a transfer, and no rate anywhere in the system is set to defend the peg
- two multisigs hold the constructive authority — one may change the supported collateral set and the custodian set, the other may grant and revoke every operational role — and no delay applies to either
- the administrator may remove any token except the protocol's own unit from the contract to an address the protocol controls

**Liquity (V1 + V2)** (13):

- in V1 the borrower pays a one-time fee at origination whose level rises with recent redemption activity and decays back, floored at half a per cent and capped at five, and pays no interest at all thereafter
- in V2 each borrower chooses their own annual interest rate and may change it whenever they like, and that same rate fixes their place in the redemption queue: redemptions consume the lowest-rate positions in a branch first, ties broken last-in-first-redeemed
- interest on each position is computed simply on its own recorded debt at its own rate and compounded only when the position is touched, while the branch keeps two running aggregates so that pending interest for the whole branch can be computed without iterating positions
- in V2 redemption volume is allocated across branches in proportion to each branch's debt minus that branch's own stability-pool deposits, so the least self-insured market absorbs the most redemption pressure
- redemption carries a fee equal to half a per cent plus a base rate that rises with redemption volume and decays on a six-hour half-life, and in V2 that fee is retained inside the redeemed borrower's collateral rather than paid to anyone
- in V2 liquidation is attempted in three ordered tiers with different payers and different penalties: offset against the stability pool at five per cent, then a just-in-time liquidation in which a liquidator supplies the stablecoin for a hundred and five per cent of the collateral value, then redistribution
- in V1, when the system-wide total collateral ratio falls below one hundred and fifty per cent the whole system changes regime: positions under 150% become liquidatable, any transaction that would worsen the aggregate ratio is blocked, and the origination fee drops to zero to pull collateral in
- in V2 each branch degrades on its own: below a critical ratio it blocks withdrawals, new debt and premature rate changes, and below a lower shutdown ratio it closes permanently to new borrowing and switches redemption to zero fee with a two per cent collateral bonus
- a borrower may delegate the choice of their own interest rate to a registered manager who declares a minimum and maximum band, may do nothing else whatsoever, and reprices the whole delegated set in one operation
- the option to reprice is itself priced: opening or changing a rate costs seven days of the borrower's own chosen interest, changing it again within seven days costs a further fee, switching manager costs an upfront fee, and a manager's own annual fee can be lowered but never raised
- a position redeemed below the minimum debt is not closed: it enters a state in which it can no longer be redeemed against but still exists and still accrues interest
- the debt position is a transferable non-fungible token, so one address may hold many of them and any of them may be sold
- the contracts cannot be changed: V1 has no administrative key, no governance and no upgrade path, and V2's core contracts are immutable and non-upgradeable while a governance system exists that can do exactly one thing

**Lista CDP** (8):

- that price is taken from an ordered chain of providers — a main source, a pivot and a fallback, drawn from four independent networks and differing per asset — and is then checked against a hard per-asset band and rejected outright if it falls outside it
- the borrow rate is recomputed every fifteen minutes, and on any user interaction, as an exponential function of the deviation of the stablecoin's price from one dollar read from an exchange oracle, parameterised per collateral by a base rate and an amplification factor, and clipped at twenty per cent
- the seized collateral is sold by an auction that opens at the unit price times 1.02 and declines linearly toward zero over a fixed horizon, pauses when it has run past a time bound or fallen about forty per cent, and must then be restarted by someone who is paid for restarting it
- that swap is free in one direction and taxed two per cent in the other, is capped in size, is subject to a daily redemption ceiling of five hundred thousand units, and is documented as taxed on exit in order to push exit onto a third-party automated market maker
- the solvency of that minted supply then depends on two lending markets the protocol neither operates nor governs, and the rates its unit earns on those markets are themselves managed by its own controller
- the rate that pool pays is a fixed number adjusted by hand, inside the same protocol whose borrow rate is set by a closed-loop controller
- parameters are changed by an off-chain vote on a hosted platform in which only core team members may submit a proposal, voting runs three days, a proposal passes on more than half of the tokens cast, and implementation follows by hand one to two weeks later
- the protocol accepts its own liquid-staking receipt as one of the assets backing its own stablecoin, so that one of its products' liabilities is another of its products' collateral

**Sky (Sky Lending, ex-MakerDAO)** (9):

- the level of the borrow rate, of the savings rate and of the savings-reserve rate is a written number: no utilisation curve, market, auction, target or measured quantity derives it anywhere in the system
- that agent may write only parameters drawn from an enumerated set of rate identifiers, each with its own configuration record, and cannot touch debt ceilings, collateral onboarding, liquidation parameters or anything else
- each value the agent writes must lie between a governance-set floor and ceiling for that identifier, and a write outside the band reverts
- a single update may move a rate by at most a governance-set step, and no update may occur within a cooldown of the previous one; the update then takes effect immediately
- settlement clears by a descending price: the auction opens above the oracle price, falls along a chosen curve, is bought atomically at the current price with an optional callback so the buyer needs no capital of their own, and is reset by anyone once it has run past a time bound or fallen below a price bound
- the balance sheet mechanically converts imbalance into an auction in both directions: surplus above a high-water mark is sold off in fixed lots, and a deficit beyond a fixed lot triggers an auction of newly issued governance tokens for the stablecoin
- the issuer maintains two of its own liabilities simultaneously, converts between them one-for-one and permissionlessly, and pays a different savings rate on each
- a sub-entity receives its own collateral type backed by an oracle that returns a constant price, purely so that a nominal collateral balance makes its debt ceiling reachable, and its operators then draw and repay the stablecoin into an off-protocol buffer with no vote and no delay, whitelisted per action and rate-limited
- the franchise is exercised by locking the governance token into an approval-voting contract and approving a slate; the slate holding the most approvals is promoted, and only the promoted address may schedule an action

**USDD** (8):

- the level of the borrow rate is a written number set by an authority the documentation does not name
- the advertised savings rate is administered by a published reaction function whose inputs are a seven-day moving average of competitor stablecoin yields, the United States Federal Reserve policy rate, a competitive market premium, and the protocol's own underlying yield
- the yield paid on that share is produced by deploying idle capital into third-party lending venues, where the venues, the caps and the phasing are chosen jointly by two named teams after review of market conditions and liquidity, and only the execution is on-chain
- the auction clears by a price that decays at a fixed rate per second and can be reset by anyone who is paid for resetting it
- the architecture provides for auctions that sell governance tokens when the protocol runs a deficit
- the issuer exists separately in three domains, with its own token contract and its own local collateral in each, and mints locally against local backing rather than bridging a single supply
- a core contract exists whose only job is to convert holders of the issuer's own predecessor liability into the current one
- the protocol states that its framework is community-driven and that critical changes are subject to community review and approval, and names no governable parameter, no timelock, no voting threshold and no administrative address

## Lane narrative

**What the section introduction should say.** Every member issues a unit meant to hold a peg against backing that is volatile, held by someone else, and can become worth less than the unit. The corpus records a *single* residue for the category — no price-of-credit instrument — and that turns out to be wrong in shape rather than wrong in fact.

**The finding: the rate gap is four gaps.** There are four distinct rate instruments among the five protocols, and the corpus files one under the wrong heading:

1. a **deployed bounded-delegate rate setter** — an agent sets the borrow rate, the savings rate and the savings-reserve rate within min, max and step bounds, with no executive vote;
2. an administered rate keyed to **external benchmarks**, including a central-bank policy rate;
3. a **closed-loop controller on peg error**;
4. **borrower-chosen** rates, priced per position by the borrower — which is not an instrument the protocol holds at all.

**Why (1) matters beyond this category.** It is the yield lane's delegated allocation mandate in different dress — named agent, bounded quantity, cap, step limit, revocation — bounding a *rate* rather than an allocation. Two lanes, different categories, different evidence, same five-part schema. That is the run's first cross-lane convergence and the strongest argument for a level above the element.

**Also.** The control-plane register is a bigger gap here than the rate one. One protocol's core is BUSL-1.1 until 2027-09-01. Two recorded residues for one protocol are refuted outright — its liquidation is standard, not gas-only. One protocol has no public repository for its CDP core at all, so its entire control plane is UNKNOWN.
